i_missing_proof.slots: The first case already has21 singleton entries. The second has20 singletons plus mandatory an. In either case at most one additional codeword L can exist under cap22. Every fixed entry already named contains no i.
i_missing_proof.existence: Since the complete word ain contains i, some additional i-containing code is necessary. Thus L exists and is the only possible i-containing code.
i_missing_proof.ain_obligation: Let k be the number of i units in L. Any parse of ain uses L a positive integer t times, and t*k=1. Hence t=1 and k=1. Because concatenation has no cancellation or deletion, L contains no unit outside {a,i,n}.
i_missing_proof.aiin_obligation: The complete word aiin has two i units. All other available codes contain none, and L contains one, so any parse must use L exactly twice. But aiin has only one a and one n. If L contained either a or n, two copies would already contribute at least two such units. Therefore L contains neither.
i_missing_proof.contradiction: L contains exactly one i and no other unit, so L is the singleton i. This contradicts the exact S assumption in both cases.
